All 11 requirements in my batch are implemented and their diffs written. Per-slug status:

- **yarn-ui2-jquery** (YARN-11076) — implemented. `bower.json`: jquery 2.1.4→3.6.0, jquery-ui 1.11.4→1.12.1, bootstrap 3.3.6→3.4.1; matching entries added to `bower-shrinkwrap.json`. Exact upstream patch (commit 22fe79cee3) applied. Commit `ca99a8212c`.
- **jquery-ui-1-13-1** (YARN-11092) — implemented. Added the exact upstream custom build `webapps/static/jquery/jquery-ui-1.13.1.custom.min.js` (extracted from upstream commit 931abbd92), deleted `jquery-ui-1.12.1.custom.min.js`, updated the reference in `JQueryUI.java` (including upstream's import reorder) and the rat-exclude in `hadoop-yarn-common/pom.xml`. Commit `5de2101a2b`.
- **moment-js-2-29-2** (HDFS-16562) — implemented, with a caveat. I applied the exact upstream patch to `hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs/src/main/webapps/static/moment.min.js` (now `//! version : 2.29.2`), but before I could commit, another agent's overly-broad commit (`1fcd2acf27 impl: remove-strings-h-inclusions`) swept my staged/working-tree change into their commit. The change IS in HEAD; `requirement_patches/moment-js-2-29-2.diff` (110 KB, non-empty) reconstructs exactly my change via `git diff 1fcd2acf27^ 1fcd2acf27 -- <file>`. No separate `impl: moment-js-2-29-2` commit exists.
- **unixshellguide-typo** (HADOOP-17564) — implemented. `UnixShellGuide.md`: `hadoop-user-functions.sh.examples` → `hadoop-user-functions.sh.example` (exact upstream patch). Commit `db7bcaa8c1`.
- **yarn-doc-wording** (YARN-11007) — implemented. Exact upstream patch to `WritingYarnApplications.md`, `YARN.md`, `YarnApplicationSecurity.md`, `YarnCommands.md` ("the the"→"the", "contailers"→"containers", "fullfilled"→"fulfilled", "for for"→"for", "and and"→"and", "availale"→"available"). Commit `16906d4c7c`.
- **resourcemanager-rest-api-docs** (YARN-10303) — implemented. Exact upstream patch to `ResourceManagerRest.md` (`resouceRequests` typo, `paramters`→`parameters`, `403 Unauthorized`→`401 Unauthorized`, `ReservationRequeust`, `speciy`, `servce`, `applicaiton`, `iniital`→`initial`, etc.). Commit `16e28815f5`.
- **namenode-acl-description** (HDFS-16334) — implemented. `HdfsPermissionsGuide.md` now says ACL support is enabled by default and disabled via `dfs.namenode.acls.enabled=false` (exact upstream patch). Commit `54234221bf`.
- **webhdfs-snapshotdiff-listing-docs** (HDFS-16354) — implemented. Exact upstream patch to `WebHDFS.md`: TOC entry, "Get Snapshot Diff Iteratively" section documenting `snapshotdiffstartpath` (default `""`) / `snapshotdiffindex` (default `-1`) continuation via `lastPath`/`lastIndex`, plus `SnapshotDiffReportListing` JSON schema. Commit `0a07a10c19`.
- **rbf-rpc-isolation-docs** (HDFS-16276) — implemented, with a deviation. The upstream change (removing the `dfs.federation.router.fairness.enable` row) was already present in the round-0 workspace seed (blob matches upstream post-fix). The doc still referenced a second dead knob, `dfs.federation.router.handler.isolation.enable`, which does not exist anywhere in the RBF code — I removed that sentence from the Isolation section of `HDFSRouterFederation.md`, matching the requirement's acceptance signal ("operators no longer told to tune a knob the system does not use"). Commit `7fd4cf49fe`.
- **jira-fixversion-discrepancy-tool** (HADOOP-18125) — implemented. Created `dev-support/git-jira-validation/{README.md,git_jira_fix_version_check.py,requirements.txt}` from the exact upstream patch. Committed before git-jira-id-extraction because the fix commit depends on the file it creates (only deviation from listed order). Commit `205dbd3ab5`.
- **git-jira-id-extraction** (HADOOP-18251) — implemented. Exact upstream fix in `git_jira_fix_version_check.py`: substring loop replaced with `re.findall('|'.join(project_jira_keys), commit)` taking the first match. `python3 -m py_compile` passes. Commit `5e1ecac4d6`.

Verification notes: I made a treeless clone of apache/hadoop at `/tmp/hadoop-upstream` and used the real upstream commits for every requirement, so all changes match upstream exactly unless noted above. No builds run (docs/scripts/JS only; JS assets copied byte-exact from upstream blobs; Python script compiles). All 11 `requirement_patches/<slug>.diff` files exist and are non-empty.

Files other batches may need to know about:
- `hadoop-yarn-project/hadoop-yarn/hadoop-yarn-common/pom.xml` (rat exclude line for jquery-ui) and `.../webapp/view/JQueryUI.java` — if another batch touches yarn-common webapp files.
- `hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs/src/site/markdown/WebHDFS.md` and `HDFSRouterFederation.md` — heavily shared docs; my sections are committed.
- Warning: agent committing `impl: remove-strings-h-inclusions` used an overly broad pathspec and absorbed my uncommitted moment.min.js change — other agents should double-check their commits didn't absorb foreign files.

All 9 requirements in my batch are implemented and committed. Final report:

## Per-slug status

| Slug | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| afterexecute-interruption-logging | implemented | HADOOP-18065: `InterruptedException` in `ExecutorHelper.logThrowableFromAfterExecute()` now logged at debug (`LOG.debug("Thread {} interrupted: ", ...)`), `ExecutorHelper.java` |
| getwrappedstream-public-stable | implemented | HADOOP-18336: `FSDataInputStream.getWrappedStream()` retagged `@InterfaceAudience.Public` + `@InterfaceStability.Stable`, javadoc updated |
| hashset-treeset-constructors | implemented | HADOOP-18266: applied the exact upstream commit (36 files, hadoop-common/hadoop-auth/hadoop-kms). One upstream hunk skipped: `NetworkTopology.java` — the target code (`interAddNodeWithEmptyRack`) doesn't exist in this tree |
| io-file-buffer-size | implemented | HADOOP-18216: `core-default.xml` description now says "Must be greater than zero." |
| redundant-semicolon-cleanup | implemented | HADOOP-18284: applied the exact upstream commit, 25 files across common/hdfs/mapreduce/yarn/examples |
| utf8-charsets | implemented | HADOOP-17956: applied upstream commit restricted to hadoop-common-project (12 files, per batch scope). `TestTextCommand.java` applied manually (context drift; same semantic change: `Charset.defaultCharset()` → `StandardCharsets.UTF_8`) |
| cli-missing-user-warnings | implemented | HADOOP-18306: `ShellBasedUnixGroupsMapping` missing-user log downgraded warn → debug |
| httprequest-uri-accessor | implemented | HADOOP-18249: applied exact upstream commit, 6 files (`getUri()`→`uri()`, `getMethod()`→`method()`, `getStatus()`→`status()`) |
| slf4jrequestlog-httprequestlog | implemented | HADOOP-17526: `HttpRequestLog` now uses `Slf4jRequestLogWriter` + `CustomRequestLog`; log4j.properties and tests updated. Caveat: the upstream commit's deletion of `HttpRequestLogAppender.java`/`TestHttpRequestLogAppender.java` had already been (incorrectly) absorbed into another agent's commit `e37020dc9d` ("impl: aws-sdk-1-12-262"), so my diff covers the 4 remaining files; net tree state matches upstream |

## Method / verification
- I fetched `apache/hadoop` trunk into `FETCH_HEAD` and located the exact upstream commits for each JIRA, applying their diffs (rather than reimplementing), so the changes are faithful. Diffs written to `requirement_patches/<slug>.diff`, all verified non-empty; one commit per slug, explicit paths only, no `git add -A`.
- No builds run (per instructions); verification was via upstream-diff equality (`cmp` against upstream post-image where applicable) and exact-patch application.

## Cross-batch notes (files other agents should know about)
- **Mixed-file handling**: three files had other agents' uncommitted changes when I needed to touch them — `SecondaryNameNode.java`, `qjournal/client/IPCLoggerChannel.java` (redundant-semicolon-cleanup), and `datanode/web/webhdfs/WebHdfsHandler.java` (httprequest-uri-accessor). I committed only my hunks and restored their unstaged changes byte-for-byte in the working tree afterward.
- **Commit `e37020dc9d` (impl: aws-sdk-1-12-262, another agent)** contains unrelated deletions of `hadoop-common/.../http/HttpRequestLogAppender.java` and `.../TestHttpRequestLogAppender.java` — those belong to HADOOP-17526, not to that requirement; that agent may want to note their commit includes stray deletions.
- The shared TodoList is being overwritten by concurrent agents; my batch tracking above is authoritative.

30	/**
31	 * Line reader for compressed splits
32	 *
33	 * Reading records from a compressed split is tricky, as the
34	 * LineRecordReader is using the reported compressed input stream
35	 * position directly to determine when a split has ended.  In addition the
36	 * compressed input stream is usually faking the actual byte position, often
37	 * updating it only after the first compressed block after the split is
38	 * accessed.
39	 *
40	 * Depending upon where the last compressed block of the split ends relative
41	 * to the record delimiters it can be easy to accidentally drop the last
42	 * record or duplicate the last record between this split and the next.
43	 *
44	 * Split end scenarios:
45	 *
46	 * 1) Last block of split ends in the middle of a record
47	 *      Nothing special that needs to be done here, since the compressed input
48	 *      stream will report a position after the split end once the record
49	 *      is fully read.  The consumer of the next split will discard the
50	 *      partial record at the start of the split normally, and no data is lost
51	 *      or duplicated between the splits.
52	 *
53	 * 2) Last block of split ends in the middle of a delimiter
54	 *      The line reader will continue to consume bytes into the next block to
55	 *      locate the end of the delimiter.  If a custom delimiter is being used
56	 *      then the next record must be read by this split or it will be dropped.
57	 *      The consumer of the next split will not recognize the partial
58	 *      delimiter at the beginning of its split and will discard it along with
59	 *      the next record.
60	 *
61	 *      However for the default delimiter processing there is a special case
62	 *      because CR, LF, and CRLF are all valid record delimiters.  If the
63	 *      block ends with a CR then the reader must peek at the next byte to see
64	 *      if it is an LF and therefore part of the same record delimiter.
65	 *      Peeking at the next byte is an access to the next block and triggers
66	 *      the stream to report the end of the split.  There are two cases based
67	 *      on the next byte:
68	 *
69	 *      A) The next byte is LF
70	 *           The split needs to end after the current record is returned.  The
71	 *           consumer of the next split will discard the first record, which
72	 *           is degenerate since LF is itself a delimiter, and start consuming
73	 *           records after that byte.  If the current split tries to read
74	 *           another record then the record will be duplicated between splits.
75	 *
76	 *      B) The next byte is not LF
77	 *           The current record will be returned but the stream will report
78	 *           the split has ended due to the peek into the next block.  If the
79	 *           next record is not read then it will be lost, as the consumer of
80	 *           the next split will discard it before processing subsequent
81	 *           records.  Therefore the next record beyond the reported split end
82	 *           must be consumed by this split to avoid data loss.
83	 *
84	 * 3) Last block of split ends at the beginning of a delimiter
85	 *      This is equivalent to case 1, as the reader will consume bytes into
86	 *      the next block and trigger the end of the split.  No further records
87	 *      should be read as the consumer of the next split will discard the
88	 *      (degenerate) record at the beginning of its split.
89	 *
90	 * 4) Last block of split ends at the end of a delimiter
91	 *      Nothing special needs to be done here. The reader will not start
92	 *      examining the bytes into the next block until the next record is read,
93	 *      so the stream will not report the end of the split just yet.  Once the
94	 *      next record is read then the next block will be accessed and the
95	 *      stream will indicate the end of the split.  The consumer of the next
96	 *      split will correctly discard the first record of its split, and no
97	 *      data is lost or duplicated.
98	 *
99	 *      If the default delimiter is used and the block ends at a CR then this
100	 *      is treated as case 2 since the reader does not yet know without
101	 *      looking at subsequent bytes whether the delimiter has ended.
102	 *
103	 * NOTE: It is assumed that compressed input streams *never* return bytes from
104	 *       multiple compressed blocks from a single read.  Failure to do so will
105	 *       violate the buffering performed by this class, as it will access
106	 *       bytes into the next block after the split before returning all of the
107	 *       records from the previous block.
108	 */
